# Lift kits and suspension lifts

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Release lines, position blocks under the truck body no more than two inches high to slide them between lower parts and stock bushings. [t755]

[Partial] Jack up the truck, allow suspension droop, then install shims with U-bolts on the spring perch. [t373]

Weigh the fully loaded vehicle to calculate rear axle weight for ordering appropriately rated springs. [t558]

[Partial] Install drop brackets to cut the second rear front crossmember on the Xterra for a 5-inch lift. [t829]

[Partial] Replace the rear leaf springs with a unit containing an additional fifth leaf. [t548]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Jack up the truck to support the frame on jackstands.
2. Allow the suspension to fully droop.

_Procedure reported by [t373]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t558] [Partial]</summary>

1. Weigh the vehicle on a scale while it is fully loaded for wheeling conditions.
2. Calculate the total weight currently sitting on the rear axle.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t829] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install drop brackets to raise the frame and body.
2. [Partial] Cut the second (rear) front crossmember on the Xterra to accommodate the bracket.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t548] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Replace the rear leaf springs with a unit containing an additional fifth leaf.
2. This addition compensates for sagging caused by extra weight compared to the original Frontier pickup design.

</details>

## Specifications

- **Block bolt torque spec**: 45 ft/lb [t755] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Body lift height per side**: 2 inches [t755] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Lift height**: 5 inch [t829] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Machine the blocks so the machined side faces toward the inside of the truck to clear the seating area slope. [t755]
- [Partial] Ensure all components are lined up before tightening everything down completely. [t755]
- Orient the larger end of the shim facing the front of the truck to tilt the axle housing upward. [t373]
- Stock 2nd gen Xterra rear axle weighs approximately 2120 lbs unloaded. [t558]
- Aim to order springs rated for a load slightly higher than your current loaded weight to prevent excessive settling. [t558]
- The curved center of the SLR bracket provides extra ground clearance in the middle. [t829]
- [Partial] Drop brackets raise suspension travel while keeping front driveline specs within factory limits. [t829]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Ordering springs that are too soft (e.g., +450 or +600) if the vehicle is heavily modified with a Titan axle and roof rack. [t558]
- [Partial] Choosing spring lengths over 4 inches which can cause arch issues on short second-gen Xterra leafs. [t558]
